title: Demo: Math models
description: Counters, base-ten blocks, number lines, fraction bars, a clock and coins, in lessons and in practice questions.
author: Erudior

lessons.title: Counters, blocks and number lines
lessons.body:
Math models let you **see** numbers. Tap the pieces or use the buttons under each model.

## Counters in a ten-frame

A ten-frame holds 10 counters: two rows of five. Add counters and count them.

```manipulative counters
count: 3
caption: Add counters until the frame shows 7.
```

Two colors help you add. Red and yellow together make the total.

```manipulative counters
frames: 2
colors: 2
count: 8
count2: 5
caption: 8 red + 5 yellow. Fill the first frame to make a ten: how many are left over?
```

## Base-ten blocks

A small cube is **one**. A rod is **ten** ones. A flat is **ten tens**: one hundred.

```manipulative blocks
value: 124
caption: This shows 124. Break a ten into 10 ones. Is it still 124?
```

```manipulative blocks
places: 4
value: 1036
caption: Thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
```

## Number lines

Hop along the line. Each hop is drawn as an arc.

```manipulative numberline
min: -10
max: 10
at: 2
hops: 1, 5
caption: Start at 2. Hop back 5. Where do you land?
```

```manipulative numberline
min: 0
max: 2
step: 1/4
caption: Fourths between 0 and 2.
```

lessons.title: Fractions, time and money
lessons.body:
## Fraction bars

Every bar is the same length, so you can compare the shaded parts.

```manipulative fractions
bars: 1/2, 0/4
caption: Shade the second bar to match 1/2. How many fourths is that?
```

```manipulative fractions
bars: 0/1
caption: Split the bar into parts, then shade some of them.
```

## Telling time

The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes.

```manipulative clock
time: 3:00
caption: Move the minute hand around once. Watch the hour hand move too.
```

## Coins

```manipulative coins
coins: penny, nickel, dime, quarter, half, dollar
start: quarter, dime
caption: Add coins to make one dollar.
```

questions.explanation: Five counters fill the top row of a ten-frame.

questions.stem: Show 6 + 3 with 6 red counters and 3 yellow counters.
questions.explanation: 6 red and 3 yellow make 9 in all.
347 is 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 7 ones. Other ways, like 34 tens and 7 ones, also make 347.

questions.stem: The blocks show 28. Add 15 more, then trade so no place has more than 9 blocks.
questions.explanation: 28 + 15: 8 ones + 5 ones = 13 ones. Trade 10 ones for a ten: 4 tens and 3 ones = 43.

questions.stem: Move the marker to -3 on the number line.
questions.explanation: -3 is 3 steps to the left of 0.
Each step is 1/4. Three steps from 0 is 3/4.
The bar has 4 equal parts. Shade 3 of them.

questions.stem: Shade the second bar to show a fraction equal to 2/3.

questions.explanation: At 2:45 the minute hand points at 9, and the hour hand is most of the way from 2 to 3.
2 quarters (50¢) + 1 dime (60¢) + 1 nickel (65¢) + 3 pennies = 68¢. That's 7 coins.

questions.stem: Make 41¢ with coins. Any coins that add up to 41¢ are right.
questions.explanation: For example: 1 quarter, 1 dime, 1 nickel and 1 penny.
